newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia-Japan steam coal price cut $2.60/t.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia-Japan steam coal price cut $2.60/t.

text.p: Australian steaming coal producers have settled with Japan for a price cut of US$2.60 to US$2.70 a tonne for exports in the 1997/98 Japanese fiscal year ending March 31, senior coal industry sources told Reuters.
The settlement was reached in talks in Cairns, Queensland, between four lead negotiating companies from Australia and Japan's lead negotiator, Chubu Electric Power Co.
The settlement will be announced in Tokyo and Nagoya by Chubu next week. Until then all parties are bound by secrecy provisions.
The new steaming coal price falls into the pattern of disappointing price results from this year's round of Australia-Japan coal price negotiations.
Hard coking coal prices were on average rolled-over, while semi-soft coking coal prices cut by US$2.00-$3.00 a tonne.
The steaming coal settlement completes the round of Australia-Japan steelmaking raw materials pricing negotiations for 1997/98.
As part of nearly three months of negotiations, iron ore prices were increased marginally, by 1.1 percent for fines while lump ore prices were unchanged.
The new steaming price brings the benchmark thermal coal price price back to less than US$30.00 a tonne for the standard grade 670 kilocalories (kcals) per kg.
At a US$2.60 a tonne price cut the new benchmark emerges at $37.70 a tonne. At a $2.70 price cut it emerges at $37.60.

The price cut involves about 40.0 percent of Australia's exported coal. The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) most recently forecast that Australia would export a total value of A$7.9 billion worth of coal in 1997, with A$3.1 billion of this in steaming coal.
Australia was forecast to export a total of 66.7 million tonnes of steaming coal in 1997, most of it to Japan.
The Australia-Japan steaming coal price will be the most powerful force in setting the Asia-Pacific market for thermal coal in 1997.
Australia's lead negotiators in this year's round were QCT Resources Ltd, MIM Holdings Ltd, Shell Australia Ltd and Ulan Coal Mines Ltd.
Ulan is a partnership of Exxon Coal Australia Ltd, a subsidiary of Exxon Corp and Mitsubishi Development Pty Ltd, a subsidiary of Japan's Mitsubishi Corp.
